subject: Pricing schedule harmonization and follow-up on caps/floors/packaging
messages:
From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@mayasystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Systems Procurement <procure@mayasystems.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing schedule — proposed harmonization and a few clarifying questions

Sean — thanks for sending the draft pricing schedule. We've run it past procurement and finance and attached a single-sheet markup (Maya_Systems_Pricing_Schedule_v3.xlsx). A few items we flagged up front:  

- Section 2 (Fees): cap/floor math is clear, but the phrasing around the annual true-up and proration during ramp looks like it could trigger an unexpectedly high true-up in year 1. Can you confirm whether pro rata calculation uses calendar months or invoice months?
- Packaging SKU mapping: our product team needs a clear mapping table for SKU-to-feature-buckets — otherwise the floor calculation becomes ambiguous.
- Burst overage carveouts: we'd like a short-term burst buffer for seasonal spikes (one-time events) without triggering a permanent higher floor.

We're not comfortable approving a floor that locks our year-1 spend without a mutual smoothing mechanism. Attached is our annotated copy. Happy to hop on quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Tom Reilly
Sr. Procurement Manager
Maya Systems
[attachment: Maya_Systems_Pricing_Schedule_v3.xlsx]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@mayasystems.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule — proposed harmonization and a few clarifying questions

Tom — appreciate the detailed pass and the attachment. High-level reply while we pull in legal/finance:  

- Proration: Redwood calculates pro rata by invoice month (we bill at the end of each invoice cycle). We can add explicit language to avoid calendar-month edge cases.
- SKU mapping: good call. We'll provide a mapping appendix that ties each SKU to a bucket used for floor calculations.
- Burst buffer: we can propose a temporary smoothing buffer (three eligible events per rolling 12 months) that won't permanently increase the floor unless recurring beyond a defined threshold.

Laura / Rishi — looping you both in for proposed contract language and the finance implications of a year-1 concession (Tom is asking for smoothing and some flexibility on the floor). I'll collate and send a consolidated redline by Thursday EOD PT.

Next steps: I'll produce a single redline with a short comment sheet and a mutual action plan so procurement can circulate internally.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment referenced: pricing_schedule_master.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@mayasystems.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule — proposed harmonization and a few clarifying questions

Team / Tom — I've reviewed the Maya markup and drafted two targeted edits to insert into the pricing exhibit. I attached a .docx with tracked changes (pricing_schedule_redlines.docx). Key proposals below (legal text suggestions):

1) Temporary Smoothing Buffer (new subsection):
"For the first twelve (12) months following Commencement, Buyer is entitled to up to three (3) non-consecutive burst events during which usage above the committed floor will not be counted toward the following period's committed minimum, provided that any single burst event represents no more than 30% above Buyer’s baseline monthly usage. Such burst events will not, by themselves, trigger a permanent recalculation of the committed minimum unless Buyer’s rolling 12-month average usage exceeds the committed floor by greater than 20% for three (3) consecutive months."

2) Proration and True-up Clarification (replace vague language):
"Proration shall be calculated on an invoice-month basis. Annual true-ups shall compare aggregate billed usage (in invoice months) to the applicable committed minimum on a 12-month rolling basis; any shortfall shall be invoiced at the base per-unit rate defined in the pricing schedule, subject to agreed caps and credit limits."

Commercial note: If Procurement requires a materially lower Year-1 floor, we should consider a visible concession (one-time volume credit or elevated discount in Year 1) rather than an opaque mechanism. Rishi, please provide guidance on quantum that finance can approve without escalation.

--
Laura Bennett
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[attachment: pricing_schedule_redlines.docx]

From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@mayasystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Systems Procurement <procure@mayasystems.com>, Kevin Li <kevin.li@mayasystems.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Aug 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule — proposed harmonization and a few clarifying questions

Laura / Sean — thanks for the language. Procurement accepts the temporary smoothing buffer in principle but has one commercial counter to balance risk to Maya's finance team: a lower Year-1 committed floor (we propose 60% of the baseline) in exchange for a 15% volume-weighted effective discount on billable units in Year 1 and a firm timetable for introducing the SKU mapping appendix within 30 days of contract execution.

We also requested explicit revenue protection language for Redwood (so you don't get under-indexed if we grow quickly) — suggested approach: a mid-year true-up trigger that allows Redwood to invoice an interim true-up if rolling 6-month usage exceeds committed floor by 40%.

We attached a short counter-proposal PDF for reference (Maya_counter_proposal_20280809.pdf). Please confirm whether Finance will accept the 15% Year-1 concession or whether we need to route to execs.

Tom
Sr. Procurement Manager
Maya Systems
[attachment: Maya_counter_proposal_20280809.pdf]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@mayasystems.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule — proposed harmonization and a few clarifying questions

Tom — thanks. Consolidated response and proposed mutual action plan below.

1) Legal language: Laura’s smoothing buffer and proration text are acceptable to us as a starting position. We will insert the language into the pricing exhibit and circulate a single tracked redline for signature.

2) Year-1 commercial trade: Finance (Rishi) indicates Redwood can approve a time-limited commercial concession of up to a 12% volume-weighted discount in Year 1 without exec escalation, provided the following are in place: (a) the Year-1 floor is set at no less than 65% of baseline; (b) the SKU mapping appendix is delivered within 30 days post-execution; (c) a mid-year 6-month rolling true-up clause (as you suggested) is included to protect Redwood in the case of rapid growth.

3) Interim true-up wording: we can accept the proposal to allow an interim invoice for a 6-month rolling overage exceeding 40% of the committed minimum; any interim invoice will be credited against the annual true-up.

Action items and timing: 
- (SEAN) Produce a single tracked redline containing Laura’s language, the agreed commercial trade, and the mid-year true-up wording — deliver by Fri, 2028-08-18.
- (MAYA) Confirm acceptance of the 65% floor / 12% discount trade and confirm procurement’s sign-off path by Tue, 2028-08-22.
- (MAYA) Deliver SKU mapping appendix within 30 days of execution.
- (LEGAL/FINANCE) Rishi / Laura to confirm final language and finance accounting treatment for the Year-1 credit before signature.

If Maya confirms the 65%/12% trade, I'll prepare a DocuSign envelope and the final signature-ready exhibit. Sharing HubSpot deal link for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8291.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment placeholder: final_pricing_exhibit_for_signature.pdf]
